claims.statement: The Python side is a virtual uv workspace whose members are listed explicitly as libs/chess, libs/systemone, libs/cli, apps/server and evals, because a glob over apps/ would include apps/web, which has no pyproject.toml.

The pnpm workspace contains apps/web, apps/review, evals/reports and packages/* (not apps/server, which has no package.json), and a shared version catalog in pnpm-workspace.yaml keeps the apps and packages/chess-ui from drifting on shared dependencies.

langchain-chess-systemone depends on langchain-chess; its SystemOneMiddleware builds on ChessMiddleware, ChessState and PositionView, and its ranker records calls using langchain_chess pricing and state types.

langchain-chess does not import langchain_chess_systemone; its only reverse link is an optional `systemone` extra that installs the sibling package, which the CLI uses via `langchain-chess[systemone]`.

Agent assembly is shared: langchain_chess_systemone.agent.build_agent turns a ChessContext into the graph for every surface, calling only the factories the policy uses (no chat model for policy 'systemone'), adding SystemOneMiddleware for any policy but 'llm', and for 'llm' adding NoSystemOne only when fixed_topology=True; both the CLI's uci/play commands and the server's build_graph call it instead of keeping their own build_agent.
The CLI's grade command reuses langchain_chess.engine and langchain_chess.grading from the core library rather than implementing grading itself.
langchain-chess-server is a private, never-published distribution (classifier `Private :: Do Not Upload`), and the CLI exposes the `lcchess` script from langchain_chess_cli.main:app.

apps/web, apps/review and evals/reports all depend on @langchain-chess/chess-ui via workspace:*, and chess-ui's package exports point directly at TypeScript source (src/index.ts, src/styles.css, src/testing.ts) with no build step.

apps/web reaches the Python agent only over HTTP: it drives the `chess` graph with useStream from @langchain/react through a session-aware SDK client, calls GET /ui/model (max_input_tokens and takes_effort) to decide whether to offer memory and a reasoning effort, and checks access with POST /assistants/search (only 401/403 count as refusal); it takes context defaults (DEFAULT_CONTEXT) from chess-ui rather than fetching /ui/config.

apps/review does not talk to the agent; it reaches only the LangSmith API through window.langsmith.call, reading threads, each game's last root run and the grader's game_review feedback, and its Analyze action writes a grade_status mark and launches `lcchess grade --sandbox-job` in a LangSmith sandbox; because it depends on chess-ui via workspace:* it can only be built from a checkout of this repo.

The TS state types in packages/chess-ui/src/types.ts are hand-maintained mirrors of langchain_chess/state.py and langchain_chess_systemone/types.py, while the settings types they use come from the generated ./generated/settings module; the server's `setup` state key is typed as unknown and read with loadRecorded.

Workspace sources (`workspace = true`) are declared only in the root pyproject.toml so `uvx --from git+…#subdirectory=libs/cli` resolves unpublished siblings from the same commit; member-level workspace sources fail in the Agent Server image because each member is installed on its own there.

The Agent Server image builds from the uv workspace with langchain-chess-server as the package; langgraph.json's dockerfile_lines ADD the pyproject.toml of libs/chess, libs/systemone, libs/cli and apps/server (not evals), and it wires the `chess` graph to graph.py:make_graph, the custom auth handler to auth.py:auth with allow_langsmith_api_keys enabled, and the HTTP app to app.py:app.

The web app's Vite build outputs by default into apps/server/langchain_chess_server/static (overridable with OUT_DIR/BASE_PATH for GitHub Pages, which hosts the deployed UI); the server mounts that directory at /ui as StaticFiles only when it exists, otherwise /ui/ returns a 404 'UI not built' response while /ui/config and /ui/model still answer.
Python tests run from the root over all five packages' test directories with 100% branch coverage required across all five import packages, and tests marked live or e2e are excluded by default.

The server injects its own ranker factory (pooled_ranker): for an `openai/` System 1 model its GatewayRanker uses an OpenAI Decisions classifier from langchain_chess_systemone.ranker.classifier with httpx clients from DECISIONS_POOL, and otherwise a langchain_typesafe TypeSafeClassifier with API key and base URL from ServerSettings.typesafe() (TYPESAFE_API_KEY and TYPESAFE_BASE_URL) and httpx2 clients from POOL; both process-wide pools are closed by the /ui app's lifespan, whereas the CLI uses build_agent's default_ranker, a plain GatewayRanker.

The shared build_agent keeps memory on only when there is a chat model and raises ChessContractError when memory is requested for a chat model with no known input limit (per langchain_chess.middleware.summarization.input_limit).

Chat models are built with the core langchain_chess.chat_models.chat_model factory: build_agent's default_model uses it for the CLI, and the server's server_model uses it with model arguments restricted to the 'server' surface.

The server's make_graph returns a model-free shape() graph (NoSystemOne plus GameSetupMiddleware, fixed topology) when there is no execution runtime, because every factory call must build the same nodes and state schema; a setting may switch a node off but never remove it.
The server-only GameSetupMiddleware records the run's resolved ChessContext as a non-private `setup` state key on a game's first turn only, so any client can continue a game from its thread.

The repository separates graph-building libraries (libs/chess with create_chess_agent, libs/systemone with SystemOneMiddleware) from clients: the web UI and Studio reach the Agent Server over HTTP, while the terminal UI and UCI engine use the agent in-process, and grading and the review app work through LangSmith.

Settings types flow from Python to TypeScript by code generation, not by runtime import: `python -m langchain_chess_server.codegen` (mise run generate:settings) renders settings.ts, settings.schema.json and opponent.schema.json into packages/chess-ui/src/generated from ChessContext's schemas, version defaults and the model_kwargs rules, and chess-ui re-exports the generated module.

The generated settings files are committed, and apps/server/tests/test_codegen.py fails when they differ from the current codegen output, so a Python settings change must regenerate and commit them in the same change.

langchain-chess-evals is a private leaf package that depends on langchain-chess and langchain-chess-systemone (using GatewayRanker, ChessContext settings files and langchain_chess grading/rules) and exposes the lcchess-evals script; no other package imports langchain_chess_evals.

ChessContext, the versioned settings model for every surface, lives in libs/systemone and extends langchain_chess.settings.CoreSettings; the CLI builds it from an optional settings file overlaid with flags, and the server resolves it from assistant context then configurable.

The server's build_graph passes GameSetupMiddleware as extra middleware, fixed_topology=True and context_schema=ChessContextInput to build_agent, and attaches the settings as sent for the server surface as run metadata.

The web app's sign-in lives entirely in the apps/web/src/auth/ module (build config from VITE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID / VITE_LANGSMITH_ORGANIZATION_ID / VITE_LANGSMITH_SSO_SLUG, the Session type and its none/x-api-key/Bearer headers, the oidc-client-ts LangSmith OAuth flow, the access check, SignIn and useSession); Root.tsx composes them and renders App only when signed in, passing it the Session.

The server's auth handler (apps/server auth.py) verifies Bearer tokens against LangSmith's JWKS with pyjwt and admits only tokens issued to the configured OAuth client for the allowed organization; requests without an Authorization header are left to LangSmith's API-key check via allow_langsmith_api_keys.
